ru: разбивать, разбить; вдребезги разбить; крушить, разгромить
separable: separable — *smash up the car*, and *smash the car up*; a pronoun has to sit in the middle: *smash it up*, never ✗ *smash up it*
gloss: To damage something badly by hitting it or crashing it.
examples: He *smashed up* his father's truck the week he got his license.
Kids *smash up* that bus shelter every spring.
The rental came back *smashed up* along one side.

ru: выкуривать, выкурить; выводить, вывести на чистую воду
separable: separable — *smoke out the informant*, *smoke the informant out*, *smoke him out*; never ✗ *smoke out him*
gloss: To force a person or a fact out of hiding.
examples: Reporters *smoked out* the source of the leak.
The new audit rules *smoke out* companies that round their numbers.
They're *smoking out* whoever has been taking supplies.

separable: separable — *smooth over the argument*, *smooth the argument over*, *smooth it over*; the set phrase *smooth things over* is the commonest form of all
gloss: To make a disagreement seem less serious so that people stop being angry.
examples: She *smoothed over* the argument with a joke.
He's always *smoothing things over* between his parents.
Somebody has to *smooth it over* before Monday.

separable: separable — *smooth out the details*, *smooth the details out*, *smooth them out*
gloss: To get rid of the small problems in something so that it runs evenly.
examples: We still need to *smooth out* a few details in the contract.
They *smoothed out* the delivery schedule last week.
The update is *smoothing out* the bugs people complained about.
contrast: *Smooth out* fixes the wrinkles in a plan; *smooth over* calms the people the plan upset.

ru: выходить, выйти (из состояния); брать себя в руки, взять себя в руки
separable: inseparable — the object follows all three words: *snap out of it*, never ✗ *snap it out of*
gloss: To stop suddenly being sad, moody, or lost in thought.
examples: *Snap out of* it — we leave in twenty minutes.
He *snapped out of* his funk the second the music started.
She hasn't been *snapping out of* these moods the way she used to.
contrast: *Snap* doubles its consonant: *snapped*, *snapping*.

separable: separable — *snap up the tickets*, *snap the tickets up*, *snap them up*; never ✗ *snap up them*
gloss: To buy or take something quickly, before someone else can get it.
examples: Fans *snap up* the cheap seats within minutes.
A developer *snapped up* the lot before it was even listed.
Shoppers were *snapping up* everything on the clearance rack.

ru: подкрадываться, подкрасться (к кому-л.); незаметно подступать, подступить
separable: inseparable — the person comes after *on*: *sneak up on her*, never ✗ *sneak her up on*
gloss: To come close to someone quietly so that they do not notice until you are there.
examples: Don't *sneak up on* me like that.
The cat *sneaked up on* the bird and missed anyway.
Finals are *sneaking up on* us.
contrast: In American speech the past is very often *snuck up on*; *sneaked up on* is the form to write.

ru: улизнуть, ускользать, ускользнуть; тайком уходить, уйти
separable: no object — *sneak out the back door*; the two words never come apart
gloss: To leave a place quietly so that nobody sees you go.
examples: We *sneaked out* after the second act.
He *sneaks out* every Friday once his parents are asleep.
They were *sneaking out* when the alarm went off.

separable: no object — *sneak in through the side door*; nothing stands between *sneak* and *in*
gloss: To get into a place quietly without being seen or without paying.
examples: They *sneaked in* through the loading dock.
He *sneaks in* late and hopes nobody notices.
Two of them were *sneaking in* when security walked by.

separable: separable — *sneak in a nap*, *sneak a nap in*, *sneak one in*
gloss: To manage to fit something small in quietly, often where there is no room for it.
examples: I *sneaked in* a run before the rain.
She always *sneaks in* one more question at the end.
He was *sneaking in* a few extra charges at the bottom of the invoice.
contrast: With no object it means to enter unseen; with an object it means to squeeze something quietly into a schedule or a list.

ru: разнюхивать, разнюхать; выискивать, выискать; находить, найти
separable: separable — *sniff out the truth*, *sniff the truth out*, *sniff it out*
gloss: To find something hidden by searching for it carefully.
examples: Auditors *sniff out* the accounts that don't add up.
She *sniffed out* the best taco truck in the city.
He has a gift for *sniffing out* talent.

ru: вынюхивать, разнюхивать; ходить вокруг да около
separable: no object, or a place after the particle — *sniff around the office*; never ✗ *sniff the office around*
gloss: To look quietly for information, especially where you are not welcome.
examples: A reporter has been *sniffing around* the department all week.
Investors *sniff around* long before they make an offer.
Someone *sniffed around* our files last month.

ru: шпионить, подглядывать; рыскать, совать нос в чужие дела
separable: no object, or a place after the particle — *snoop around my desk*; never ✗ *snoop my desk around*
gloss: To look through someone's private things or business without permission.
examples: I caught him *snooping around* my desk.
She *snooped around* the house while we were out.
Kids *snoop around* for presents every December.

ru: гасить, погасить; подавлять, подавить; обрывать, оборвать
separable: separable — *snuff out the candle*, *snuff the candle out*, *snuff it out*
gloss: To put a sudden end to something, or to put out a small flame.
examples: He *snuffs out* the candles before bed.
One bad quarter *snuffed out* the company's expansion plans.
The protest was *snuffed out* within a day.

separable: no object — the person you move toward follows *to* or *against*: *snuggle up to her*
gloss: To move close to someone or something for warmth and comfort.
examples: The kids *snuggle up* on the couch to watch cartoons.
She *snuggled up* to him under the blanket.
The dog was *snuggling up* against my leg.

separable: separable — *soak up the spill*, *soak the spill up*, *soak it up*
gloss: To take in a liquid, or to remove it with something absorbent.
examples: Use a dish towel to *soak up* the spill.
The bread *soaked up* the last of the sauce.
Paper towels were *soaking up* the water under the sink.

separable: separable — *soak up the sun*, *soak it up*; with a long object the two words usually stay together: *soaking up the atmosphere of the old town*
gloss: To take in and enjoy something around you, such as sunshine, atmosphere, or new knowledge.
examples: We sat on the porch *soaking up* the sun.
She *soaks up* languages faster than anyone I know.
They *soaked up* the atmosphere at the night market.
contrast: One verb, two worlds: a sponge *soaks up* water, a traveler *soaks up* a city.

separable: separable when there is an object — *sober him up*, *sober up the whole crew*; with no object it stands alone: *he sobered up by noon*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*he sobered up by noon*), transitive (*coffee sobered him up*)
gloss: To stop being drunk, or to make someone stop being drunk.
examples: He needs an hour to *sober up* before he drives.
Black coffee *sobered him up* enough to talk.
They were still *sobering up* at lunchtime.

ru: задабривать, задобрить; смягчать, смягчить (кого-л.); уговаривать, уговорить
separable: separable — *soften up the boss*, *soften the boss up*, *soften her up*; never ✗ *soften up her*
gloss: To make someone more willing to agree, usually by being nice to them first.
examples: Take her to dinner and *soften her up* before you ask.
The salesman *softened us up* with free samples.
He's been *softening up* his parents all week.

separable: separable — *sort out the problem*, *sort the problem out*, *sort it out*; never ✗ *sort out it*
gloss: To deal with a problem or a confused situation until it is settled.
examples: We need to *sort out* the billing mistake today.
They *sorted out* their differences over lunch.
I'm still *sorting out* what actually happened.

separable: separable — *sort out the winter clothes*, *sort the winter clothes out*, *sort them out*
gloss: To separate a group of things and put them in order or into piles.
examples: *Sort out* the winter clothes and donate the rest.
She *sorted out* the mail into three piles.
He was *sorting out* his tools when I called.
contrast: Both meanings are separable, and with a pronoun you have no choice at all: *sort it out*.

separable: inseparable — the pile follows the particle: *sort through the mail*, never ✗ *sort the mail through*
gloss: To look at every item in a pile in order to find something or decide what to keep.
examples: I spent Sunday *sorting through* old photographs.
She *sorted through* a hundred applications in two days.
We *sort through* the donations every Friday.
contrast: *Sort out* finishes the job; *sort through* is the going-item-by-item part of it.

separable: no object — the topic follows *about* or *on*: *sound off about taxes*
gloss: To say loudly and at length what you think, especially to complain.
examples: He *sounds off* about taxes at every family dinner.
She *sounded off* in the comments for an hour.
They were *sounding off* about the new parking rules.

separable: separable — *sound out the team*, *sound the team out*, *sound them out*
gloss: To find out carefully what someone thinks before you make a decision public.
examples: *Sound out* the team before you announce anything.
He *sounded out* a few donors last month.
She's *sounding out* investors quietly.

ru: отключаться, отключиться; витать в облаках; терять, потерять нить
separable: no object — *I spaced out*; the two words never come apart in this meaning
gloss: To stop paying attention and stare at nothing for a while.
examples: I *spaced out* during the whole second half.
He *spaces out* the moment numbers come up.
Sorry, I was *spacing out* — say that again?

ru: произносить, произнести по буквам; писать, написать полностью
separable: separable — *spell out your name*, *spell your name out*, *spell it out*
gloss: To say or write the letters of a word one at a time.
examples: Could you *spell out* your last name for me?
She *spelled out* the street name twice.
He's *spelling out* the address for the driver.
contrast: American English writes *spelled*; *spelt* is British.

ru: разъяснять, разъяснить; растолковывать, растолковать; чётко прописывать, прописать
separable: separable — *spell out the rules*, *spell the rules out*, *spell it out*
gloss: To explain something in plain detail so that nothing is left to guess.
examples: The contract *spells out* who pays for repairs.
I had to *spell it out* for him twice.
She *spelled out* exactly what would happen if we were late.

ru: оживлять, оживить; придавать, придать остроты; разнообразить
separable: separable — *spice up the report*, *spice the report up*, *spice it up*
gloss: To make something more interesting or exciting.
examples: A few photos would *spice up* the report.
He *spiced up* the story with details that never happened.
They're *spicing up* the menu for summer.

separable: no object — where it spreads to follows *into*: *spill over into the street*
gloss: To spread beyond where it started, usually of a problem or a conflict.
examples: The argument *spilled over* into the parking lot.
Stress at work *spills over* into everything else.
Protests have been *spilling over* into nearby towns.
contrast: American English writes *spilled*; *spilt* is British.

ru: жить за чей-л. счёт; сидеть на шее; паразитировать
separable: inseparable — the person paying follows *off*: *sponge off his sister*, never ✗ *sponge his sister off*
gloss: To live on someone else's money without giving anything back.
examples: He's been *sponging off* his sister since March.
She *sponged off* friends for a year after college.
Nobody wants to *sponge off* their parents at thirty.

ru: приводить, привести в порядок; наводить, навести лоск; прихорашиваться
separable: separable — *spruce up the yard*, *spruce the yard up*, *spruce it up*; with yourself as the object: *spruce yourself up*
gloss: To make something or yourself look neater and more attractive.
examples: We *spruced up* the yard before the open house.
A coat of paint *spruces up* the whole room.
She's *sprucing herself up* for the interview.

ru: подстёгивать, подстегнуть; побуждать, побудить; воодушевлять, воодушевить
separable: separable — *spur on the runners*, *spur the runners on*, *spur them on*; a pronoun must go in the middle
gloss: To encourage someone to try harder or to keep going.
examples: The crowd *spurred them on* in the last mile.
Her success *spurs on* the younger players.
He was *spurred on* by everyone who said it couldn't be done.
contrast: *Spur* doubles the r: *spurred*, *spurring*.

ru: улаживать, уладить; приводить, привести в порядок
separable: separable — *square away the paperwork*, *square the paperwork away*, *square it away*; very often passive: *we're all squared away*
gloss: To finish arranging something so that it is settled and in order.
examples: Let me *square away* the paperwork first.
We *squared everything away* before the holiday.
Are you all *squared away* for the trip?

separable: no object on the verb — the person you pay follows *with*: *square up with him*
gloss: To pay someone what you owe them so that nobody is out of pocket.
examples: I'll *square up* with you on Friday.
We *squared up* at the end of the trip.
They're still *squaring up* after the move.

ru: вступать, вступить в противоборство; готовиться к схватке
separable: no object — the opponent follows *against* or *with*: *square off against the champion*
gloss: To get ready to fight or compete against someone.
examples: The two candidates *square off* on Thursday.
They *squared off* in the parking lot over a dent.
The teams have been *squaring off* for this title since 1998.

ru: согласовываться, согласоваться; сходиться, сойтись (с чем-л.); соответствовать
separable: inseparable — what it matches follows *with*: *square with the facts*, never ✗ *square the facts with*
gloss: To match or agree with other facts or statements.
examples: His story doesn't *square with* the receipts.
That *squared with* what the neighbor told police.
Nothing he said is *squaring with* the video.

separable: separable — *squeeze in one more patient*, *squeeze one more patient in*, *squeeze you in*
gloss: To find time or room for someone or something when there is barely enough.
examples: The dentist can *squeeze you in* at four.
We *squeezed in* a swim before dinner.
She's *squeezing in* one more meeting before her flight.

ru: вытеснять, вытеснить; выжимать, выжать; с трудом добывать, добыть
separable: separable — *squeeze out the small stores*, *squeeze the small stores out*, *squeeze them out*
gloss: To force someone or something out, or to get the last bit of something with effort.
examples: The big chains *squeezed out* the corner stores.
They *squeeze out* a win in overtime almost every year.
Rising rents are *squeezing families out* of the neighborhood.

separable: separable — *squirrel away some cash*, *squirrel some cash away*, *squirrel it away*
gloss: To hide money or supplies somewhere safe so you can use them later.
examples: She *squirrels away* a little from every paycheck.
He had *squirreled away* enough for a down payment.
They're *squirreling away* canned goods for winter.
contrast: American English keeps one l: *squirreled*, *squirreling*. British English doubles it.

separable: no object — the things pile up by themselves: *the bills stacked up*
gloss: To build up in number or in a pile, usually faster than you can deal with them.
examples: The bills *stack up* fast when you're out of work.
Emails *stacked up* while I was on vacation.
Cars were *stacking up* behind the accident.

separable: no object on the verb — what you compare it to follows *against* or *to*: *stack up against the competition*
gloss: To compare with something else in quality or value.
examples: How does the new model *stack up* against last year's?
Their offer *stacked up* poorly next to ours.
Let's see how the numbers are *stacking up*.
contrast: In the piling-up sense it stands alone; in the comparing sense it almost always drags *against* or *to* behind it.

separable: separable — *stake out the motel*, *stake the motel out*, *stake it out*
gloss: To watch a place secretly for a long time, hoping to catch someone.
examples: Detectives *staked out* the motel for three nights.
Reporters are *staking out* her house.
They *stake out* the same corner every weekend.

separable: separable — *stake out a position*, *stake a position out*, *stake it out*
gloss: To claim a position or a piece of territory publicly as your own.
examples: She *staked out* a clear position on the tax bill.
Both companies are *staking out* the same market.
He *stakes out* the same spot by the window every morning.

separable: no object — *the engine stalled out*; the two words never come apart
gloss: To stop running, or to stop making any progress.
examples: The engine *stalled out* at the light.
Talks have *stalled out* over wages.
Sales are *stalling out* in the second quarter.

separable: separable — *stamp out corruption*, *stamp corruption out*, *stamp it out*
gloss: To get rid of something bad completely.
examples: The program aims to *stamp out* measles by 2030.
They *stamped out* the rumor within a day.
We're *stamping out* the last of the fraud cases.

ru: переглядеть; смотреть в упор (пока не отступит); осаживать взглядом
separable: separable — *stare down the batter*, *stare the batter down*, *stare him down*
gloss: To look steadily at someone until they give in or look away.
examples: The pitcher *stared down* the batter.
She *stares down* anyone who questions her numbers.
He was *staring the whole room down*.
contrast: *Stare at* is just looking; *stare down* is a contest that somebody loses.

ru: начинать, начать заново; начинать с нуля
separable: no object — *start over*; nothing goes between the two words
gloss: To begin again from the beginning.
examples: The file was corrupted and I had to *start over*.
They sold everything and *started over* in Denver.
He's *starting over* at forty-five.
contrast: *Start over* is the American form; British English says *start again*.

separable: no object — *start out as a clerk*; the two words stay together
gloss: To begin a job, a journey, or a life in a particular way.
examples: She *started out* as a receptionist and runs the place now.
We *start out* at dawn if the weather holds.
It was *starting out* as a joke and turned into a business.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *start off the meeting*, *start the meeting off*, *start it off*; just as common with no object: *the day started off badly*
transitivity: both — transitive (*she started off the class with a story*), intransitive (*the day started off badly*)
gloss: To begin something, or to begin in a particular way.
examples: Let's *start off* with introductions.
She *started off* the class with a story.
The week is *starting off* better than the last one.

ru: заводить, завести; заводиться, завестись; запускать, запустить
separable: separable when it takes an object — *start up the generator*, *start the generator up*, *start it up*; the machine can also *start up* by itself
transitivity: both — transitive (*he started up the mower*), intransitive (*the furnace starts up at night*)
gloss: To make an engine or a machine begin running, or to begin running.
examples: He *started up* the mower at seven in the morning.
The furnace *starts up* whenever it drops below sixty.
My laptop is *starting up* now.

ru: открывать, открыть (дело); основывать, основать; создавать, создать
separable: separable — *start up a bakery*, *start a bakery up*, *start it up*
gloss: To create a new business or organization.
examples: They *started up* a bakery in the old post office.
She wants to *start up* her own firm.
He's *starting up* a nonprofit for veterans.
contrast: The noun *a startup* comes from this meaning, not from the engine one.

separable: inseparable — the task follows *on*: *start on the dishes*, never ✗ *start the dishes on*
gloss: To begin working on something.
examples: I'll *start on* the dishes while you cook.
She *started on* her homework right after dinner.
We're *starting on* the roof tomorrow.

ru: прятать, спрятать; откладывать, отложить; припрятывать, припрятать
separable: separable — *stash away the extra keys*, *stash the extra keys away*, *stash them away*
gloss: To put something in a safe or secret place.
examples: He *stashed away* the extra keys in a kitchen drawer.
They *stash away* a few hundred dollars every month.
She had *stashed* the letters *away* in a shoebox.

ru: предотвращать, предотвратить; отсрочивать, отсрочить; отгонять, отогнать
separable: separable — *stave off hunger*, *stave hunger off*, *stave it off*; a long object usually stays after the particle
gloss: To keep something bad away for a while, without getting rid of it for good.
examples: A snack will *stave off* hunger until dinner.
The loan *staved off* bankruptcy for another year.
They're *staving off* layoffs as long as they can.

ru: не ложиться спать; бодрствовать; засиживаться, засидеться
separable: no object — *stay up late*; nothing goes between *stay* and *up*
gloss: To go to bed later than you usually do.
examples: We *stayed up* to watch the election results.
He *stays up* too late on school nights.
I've been *staying up* reading.

ru: оставаться, остаться дома; никуда не выходить
separable: no object — *stay in tonight*
gloss: To remain at home instead of going out.
examples: Let's *stay in* tonight and order something.
They *stayed in* all weekend because of the storm.
She's been *staying in* since the surgery.

separable: no object — *stay out late*
gloss: To remain away from home, especially late at night.
examples: He *stayed out* until two in the morning.
The kids can't *stay out* past ten on a school night.
They were *staying out* every night that summer.

ru: оставаться, остаться на ночь; ночевать, переночевать
separable: no object — *stay over at a friend's house*
gloss: To spend the night at someone else's home.
examples: Can Maya *stay over* on Friday?
He *stayed over* after the party rather than drive.
The cousins are *staying over* through Sunday.

ru: оставаться, остаться (в должности, на прежнем месте)
separable: no object — *stay on another year*
gloss: To remain in a job or a place longer than planned or expected.
examples: She *stayed on* an extra year as interim dean.
Most of the crew *stay on* through the winter.
He's *staying on* until they find a replacement.

separable: inseparable — what you avoid follows *from*: *stay away from the bridge*, never ✗ *stay the bridge away from*
gloss: To deliberately avoid a person, a place, or a thing.
examples: *Stay away from* the bridge until the ice melts.
He *stayed away from* sugar for a month.
She's been *staying away from* the news.

separable: no object — *stay behind and lock up*
gloss: To remain in a place after the other people have left.
examples: Two of us *stayed behind* to clean up.
He *stays behind* after practice to shoot free throws.
She was *staying behind* to lock the doors.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *steam up the mirror*, *steam the mirror up*, *steam it up*; the glass can also *steam up* on its own
transitivity: both — intransitive (*his glasses steamed up*), transitive (*the shower steamed up the mirror*)
gloss: To cover glass with warm mist so that you cannot see through it.
examples: The bathroom mirror *steams up* every morning.
His glasses *steamed up* the moment he walked inside.
The soup was *steaming up* the kitchen window.

separable: separable — *step up patrols*, *step patrols up*, *step them up*
gloss: To increase something or do it more intensively.
examples: Police *stepped up* patrols after the break-ins.
We need to *step up* production before the holidays.
They're *stepping up* the pressure on suppliers.
contrast: *Step* doubles the p: *stepped*, *stepping*.

ru: брать, взять на себя ответственность; проявлять, проявить инициативу
separable: no object — *somebody has to step up*; in this meaning nothing follows the verb
gloss: To come forward and do what is needed, especially when nobody else will.
examples: Somebody has to *step up* and lead this project.
She *stepped up* when the manager quit.
The younger players are *stepping up* this season.
contrast: With an object it means to increase: *step up production*. With nothing after it, it means to take responsibility.

ru: уходить, уйти в отставку; слагать, сложить полномочия
separable: no object — the job follows *as* or *from*: *step down as chair*
gloss: To leave an important job or position.
examples: The CEO *stepped down* in March.
He *steps down* at the end of his term.
She's *stepping down* after twelve years on the board.

separable: no object — *step in and help*
gloss: To get involved in a situation in order to help or to stop trouble.
examples: A teacher *stepped in* before the fight started.
The state *steps in* when a district runs out of money.
His lawyer is *stepping in* to handle the negotiation.

separable: no object — *step out for a minute*
gloss: To leave a room or a building for a short time.
examples: She *stepped out* to take a call.
He *steps out* for coffee around ten every morning.
They've *stepped out* for lunch — try back at one.

ru: отстраняться, отстраниться; взглянуть со стороны; сделать шаг назад
separable: no object — *step back and look at it*
gloss: To stop and look at a situation from a distance so that you can judge it clearly.
examples: Let's *step back* and ask what the customer actually wants.
He *stepped back* from daily operations last year.
We're *stepping back* to rethink the whole design.

ru: уступать, уступить место; отходить, отойти в сторону
separable: no object — *step aside for someone younger*
gloss: To give up your position so that someone else can take it.
examples: The chairman *stepped aside* for a younger candidate.
She *steps aside* gracefully whenever someone knows the subject better.
He's *stepping aside* at the end of the season.
contrast: *Step down* is leaving the job for good; *step aside* stresses that you are making room for somebody else.

ru: вызывать, вызвать; провоцировать, спровоцировать; будоражить, взбудоражить
separable: separable — *stir up trouble*, *stir trouble up*, *stir it up*
gloss: To cause trouble or strong feelings, often deliberately.
examples: The article *stirred up* a lot of anger.
He *stirs up* trouble wherever he goes.
They've been *stirring up* the neighbors about the new building.
contrast: *Stir* doubles the r: *stirred*, *stirring*.

separable: no object on the verb itself — what you buy follows *on*: *stock up on batteries*, never ✗ *stock batteries up*
gloss: To buy a large amount of something to keep for later.
examples: People *stock up* on water before a hurricane.
We *stocked up* at the warehouse store on Sunday.
She's *stocking up* on coffee while it's on sale.

ru: заходить, зайти (ненадолго); заглядывать, заглянуть; заезжать, заехать
separable: inseparable — the place follows the particle: *stop by the store*, never ✗ *stop the store by*; with no place named it stands alone: *stop by anytime*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*stop by after work*), transitive (*stop by the office*)
gloss: To visit a place or a person briefly, often without arranging it first.
examples: *Stop by* after work if you're free.
She *stopped by* the office to drop off a check.
He's *stopping by* around six.
contrast: *Stop* doubles the p: *stopped*, *stopping*.

ru: заезжать, заехать (по пути); делать, сделать остановку
separable: no object — the place follows *at* or *in*: *stop off at the gym*
gloss: To break a journey briefly to do something before going on.
examples: We *stopped off* in Reno for gas.
She *stops off* at the gym on the way home.
They were *stopping off* to see friends.

ru: делать, сделать остановку (в пути); останавливаться, остановиться на ночь
separable: no object — the place follows *in*: *stop over in Dallas*
gloss: To break a long trip, especially a flight, and stay somewhere before going on.
examples: We *stopped over* in Dallas for six hours.
Most of those flights *stop over* in Reykjavik.
They're *stopping over* in Tokyo for two nights.
contrast: *Stop off* is a quick errand on the way; *stop over* is long enough to leave the airport, often overnight. The noun is *a stopover*.

ru: заглядывать, заглянуть; заходить, зайти на минутку
separable: no object — the person or place follows *at*, *on*, or *to see*: *stop in at the shop*
gloss: To make a short visit somewhere.
examples: *Stop in* and say hello when you're downtown.
He *stopped in* on his way to the airport.
Neighbors keep *stopping in* to check on her.

ru: засорять, засорить; затыкать, заткнуть; закупоривать, закупорить
separable: separable — *stop up the drain*, *stop the drain up*, *stop it up*; very often passive: *the sink is stopped up*
gloss: To block a pipe, a hole, or an opening so that nothing can pass through.
examples: Grease *stopped up* the kitchen drain.
*Stop up* the gap with steel wool and the mice will stay out.
Something is *stopping up* the vent.

ru: накапливать, накопить; запасать, запасти; копить в себе
separable: separable — *store up food*, *store food up*, *store it up*
gloss: To collect something and keep it for the future.
examples: Squirrels *store up* nuts all fall.
He *stored up* years of resentment and never said a word.
They're *storing up* fuel before prices rise.

ru: вылетать, вылететь (в гневе); уходить, уйти, хлопнув дверью
separable: no object — the room follows *of*: *storm out of the meeting*
gloss: To leave a place suddenly and angrily.
examples: She *stormed out* of the meeting.
He *storms out* every time the subject comes up.
They were *storming out* just as we arrived.
contrast: *Storm off* means the same thing; *storm out* is the one that names the room or building you left.

ru: убирать, убрать (на хранение); складывать, сложить; прятать, спрятать
separable: separable — *stow away your bags*, *stow your bags away*, *stow them away*
gloss: To put something away neatly where it will be out of the way.
examples: Please *stow away* your bags before takeoff.
He *stowed* the tent *away* in the garage.
We're *stowing away* the deck furniture for winter.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *straighten up the kitchen*, *straighten the kitchen up*, *straighten it up*; also used alone: *I'll straighten up before they get here*
transitivity: both — transitive (*straighten up the room*), intransitive (*I straightened up a little*)
gloss: To make a room or a pile of things neat.
examples: Can you *straighten up* the living room?
She *straightened up* while the coffee brewed.
He's *straightening up* his desk before the meeting.

ru: улаживать, уладить; исправлять, исправить; распутывать, распутать
separable: separable — *straighten out the mix-up*, *straighten the mix-up out*, *straighten it out*
gloss: To fix a confused or troublesome situation.
examples: The bank *straightened out* the double charge.
Let's *straighten this out* before it gets worse.
She's *straightening out* the schedule now.

ru: вразумлять, вразумить; наставлять, наставить на путь истинный
separable: separable — *straighten out that kid*, *straighten him out*; with a pronoun the middle is the only place it can go
gloss: To make someone stop behaving badly.
examples: A year in the army *straightened him out*.
His grandmother *straightens out* anyone who talks back.
They're hoping the new coach will *straighten out* the team.
contrast: The same verb fixes a mess and fixes a person: *straighten out the billing*, *straighten out your brother*.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *strap the baby in*, *strap her in*; used alone it means fasten your own belt: *everybody strap in*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*strap in, we're leaving*), transitive (*she strapped the twins in*)
gloss: To fasten a seat belt or harness, for yourself or for someone else.
examples: *Strap in* — this road gets rough.
She *strapped* the twins *in* and backed out of the driveway.
He was still *strapping in* when the ride started.
contrast: *Strap* doubles the p: *strapped*, *strapping*.

ru: нервировать; доводить, довести до стресса; нервничать, изводиться
separable: separable when it takes an object — *stress out the whole team*, *stress them out*; with no object it describes your own state: *don't stress out*
transitivity: both — transitive (*the deadline stressed her out*), intransitive (*he stresses out over nothing*)
gloss: To make someone very anxious, or to become very anxious.
examples: Finals *stress out* even the best students.
The move *stressed us out* for months.
He's been *stressing out* about the interview all week.

ru: растягиваться, растянуться; вытягиваться, вытянуться; растягивать, растянуть
separable: separable when it takes an object — *stretch out your legs*, *stretch your legs out*, *stretch them out*; with no object it means to lie down full length: *he stretched out on the couch*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*she stretched out on the grass*), transitive (*stretch out the dough*)
gloss: To lie down with your body extended, or to pull something out to its full length.
examples: He *stretched out* on the couch and fell asleep.
*Stretch out* your hamstrings before you run.
She was *stretching out* the last of the dough.

separable: separable — *strip down the engine*, *strip the engine down*, *strip it down*
gloss: To take a machine apart into its separate pieces.
examples: He *stripped down* the carburetor on the kitchen table.
They *strip down* every engine before the season starts.
The bike has been *stripped down* to the frame.
contrast: *Strip* doubles the p: *stripped*, *stripping*.

separable: no object — how far you undress follows *to*: *strip down to your shorts*
gloss: To take off your clothes, usually down to your underwear.
examples: The doctor asked him to *strip down* to his shorts.
They *stripped down* and jumped in the lake.
She was *stripping down* for the X-ray when the tech knocked.

separable: separable — *strip off the old paint*, *strip the old paint off*, *strip it off*
gloss: To remove a covering layer from a surface.
examples: We *stripped off* the old wallpaper in a weekend.
Salt *strips off* the paint faster than anything.
He's *stripping off* the varnish with a heat gun.

separable: inseparable — the subject follows *on*: *study up on the rules*, never ✗ *study the rules up on*
gloss: To read about a subject so that you know enough about it in advance.
examples: I need to *study up on* the new tax rules.
She *studied up on* the company before her interview.
He's been *studying up on* Italian wines.
contrast: *Study* changes y to i in *studies* and *studied*, but keeps it in *studying*.

separable: inseparable — what you find follows the particle: *stumble across an old letter*, never ✗ *stumble it across*
gloss: To find something by accident, without looking for it.
examples: I *stumbled across* her blog while looking for a recipe.
They *stumbled across* an old cemetery in the woods.
Researchers keep *stumbling across* the same error.

separable: inseparable — what you find follows *upon*: *stumble upon the answer*, never ✗ *stumble the answer upon*
gloss: To discover something by chance.
examples: He *stumbled upon* the answer while doing something else entirely.
We *stumble upon* good bands this way all the time.
She had *stumbled upon* a letter dated 1943.
contrast: *Stumble upon*, *stumble across*, and *stumble on* all mean the same; *across* and *on* are the usual ones in speech, *upon* the most formal.

separable: inseparable — the person follows *to*: *suck up to the boss*, never ✗ *suck the boss up to*
gloss: To flatter someone important in order to get something from them.
examples: He *sucks up to* every manager he meets.
She *sucked up to* the coach all season and still didn't start.
They're *sucking up to* the new owner.

separable: fixed with *it* in the middle — *suck it up*; nothing else goes there, and ✗ *suck up it* is impossible
gloss: To accept something unpleasant and stop complaining about it.
examples: *Suck it up* and finish the shift.
He *sucked it up* and apologized to her in front of everyone.
We're all just *sucking it up* until payday.
contrast: Do not confuse it with *suck up to someone*, which is flattery, not endurance.

ru: подводить, подвести итог; резюмировать; кратко излагать, изложить
separable: separable — *sum up the argument*, *sum the argument up*, *sum it up*
gloss: To state the main points of something in a short form.
examples: Let me *sum up* what we agreed on.
She *summed up* the whole report in two sentences.
That one word *sums up* the entire year.
contrast: *Sum* doubles the m: *summed*, *summing*.

separable: separable — *summon up the courage*, *summon the courage up*, *summon it up*; the usual order keeps the two words together
gloss: To find enough of a feeling such as courage or energy to do something difficult.
examples: She finally *summoned up* the nerve to ask.
He can't *summon up* much enthusiasm for the trip.
I was *summoning up* the energy to start over.

ru: экипироваться; надевать, надеть форму; облачаться, облачиться
separable: no object — *suit up before practice*; the two words stay together
gloss: To put on the uniform or protective clothing that a job or a sport requires.
examples: The team *suits up* an hour before kickoff.
Firefighters *suited up* and went in.
He's *suiting up* for his first game back.

separable: separable — *swallow up the savings*, *swallow the savings up*, *swallow them up*; often passive: *the farms were swallowed up by the city*
gloss: To take something in completely so that it disappears.
examples: Rent *swallows up* half her paycheck.
The city *swallowed up* the surrounding farms.
Legal fees were *swallowing up* the whole settlement.

separable: separable — *swap out the battery*, *swap the battery out*, *swap it out*; the replacement follows *for*: *swap it out for a new one*
gloss: To take one thing out and put another in its place.
examples: We *swapped out* the old router for a new one.
*Swap* the battery *out* and see if that helps.
They're *swapping out* the whole lighting system this month.
contrast: *Swap* doubles the p: *swapped*, *swapping*.

separable: separable — *switch on the lamp*, *switch the lamp on*, *switch it on*; never ✗ *switch on it*
gloss: To make a light or a machine start working, usually with a switch.
examples: *Switch on* the lamp — I can't see a thing.
He *switched* the radio *on* and hummed along.
She was *switching on* the porch light when we pulled up.
contrast: *Turn on* is the more common American choice; *switch on* is used when there really is a switch.

separable: separable — *switch off the lights*, *switch the lights off*, *switch them off*; never ✗ *switch off them*
gloss: To make a light or a machine stop working, usually with a switch.
examples: Please *switch off* your phones before the show.
He *switched* the engine *off* and just sat there.
The system *switches off* automatically at midnight.

separable: no object — *the class switched off*; in this meaning nothing follows the verb
gloss: To stop listening or paying attention.
examples: Students *switch off* after about twenty minutes.
I *switched off* halfway through his speech.
He's *switching off* again — look at his face.
contrast: With an object it is a machine: *switch off the TV*. With nothing after it, it is a person's attention.

separable: no object — the new thing follows *to*: *switch over to solar*
gloss: To change from one system, channel, or supplier to another.
examples: We *switched over* to solar last spring.
*Switch over* to channel four — it's already started.
The office is *switching over* to new software in June.

separable: separable — *switch out the rug*, *switch the rug out*, *switch it out*; the replacement follows *for*
gloss: To replace one thing with another of the same kind.
examples: They *switched out* the batteries in every detector.
*Switch* the rug *out* for something lighter.
She's *switching out* the summer clothes for sweaters.
contrast: *Switch out* and *swap out* are interchangeable in American speech.

separable: separable — *switch up the routine*, *switch the routine up*, *switch it up*
gloss: To change something so that it is not always done the same way.
examples: Let's *switch up* the routine this week.
The coach *switched up* the lineup after halftime.
They keep *switching up* the menu, which is why we go back.

ru: синхронизироваться; согласовывать, согласовать действия; созваниваться, созвониться
separable: no object — the person you meet follows *with*: *sync up with the design team*
gloss: To meet briefly so that everyone has the same information, or of two things, to match up.
examples: Let's *sync up* Monday morning before the call.
We *synced up* with the design team yesterday.
The two calendars aren't *syncing up*.
contrast: American English writes *synced* and *syncing*, without the h.
